summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis on Simponi, exercise-induced asthma, chronic pain, GERD, hypertension, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for an asthma exacerbation triggered by an upper respiratory infection. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, cough, and increased nebulizer use despite outpatient treatment with prednisone and azithromycin. His fever had resolved, but respiratory symptoms progressed, prompting hospitalization. He was treated with IV ceftriaxone initially, transitioned to Augmentin, continued on prednisone 60 mg daily, and received duoneb treatments. His breathing improved significantly, and he was discharged home after two days with instructions to complete antibiotics, taper prednisone by 10 mg daily, and resume home asthma medications as the flare resolved. Follow-up with his primary care provider was advised.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
